qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, criticising or thanking them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in return, whether the returned description matches the first one or is different or opposite. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

neighbours.label: On the word right after me, us or you that opens a description of that speaker or listener (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my', 'our' or 'your') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has I, we or you characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, criticising or thanking them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise the same I, we or you in return, whether the returned description matches the first one or is different or opposite. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns; named people are mostly silent. Silent: a returned attitude with no description after the pronoun (they trusted us); a returned description with no linking word, just a bare noun; a one-way characterisation with no earlier clause; the speaker characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.
fire: We had always seen the neighbours as rivals, and it turned out they saw us as rivals too.
I thought of her as a mentor, but she thought of me as a friend.
You called them cowards, so naturally they called you a bully.
We praised the volunteers for their patience, and they praised us for our organisation.
I regarded him as a genius, while he regarded me as a fool.
You thanked the nurses for their kindness, and they thanked you for your courage.
We considered the other team serious opponents, and they considered us as easy prey.
I criticised the editors for their sloppiness, and they criticised me for my stubbornness.
quiet: We had always seen the neighbours as rivals, though we never told them so.
I thought of her as a mentor, and she trusted me completely.
You called them cowards, so naturally they stopped speaking to you.
We praised the volunteers for their patience, and they smiled and went back to work.
I regarded the old house as a treasure, and it repaid me with years of shelter.
You helped the nurses move the beds, and they helped you carry the boxes.
The other team considered us easy prey, and we answered by winning the match.
We lent the farmers our tractor, and they lent us their trailer the next week.

predictions: Blind test (label-only author). Expect most fire items above 0.3; the 'called you a bully' item may be weaker; near misses near zero.
